text:
Priya - Support: Hey team, escalated ticket from AcmeCorp: customers seeing 5xx and gateway timeouts on hosted inference since ~08:12 UTC. Lots of timeouts to /v1/generate and elevated latency. Caller reports repeated 502/504. Request id: req_9f3b2c. Can SRE please triage? :rotating_light:

Ethan - SRE: I'm on it. Any customer repro steps or recent deploys?

Priya - Support: Repro steps from customer: curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -d '{"model":"redwood-large","prompt":"hello"}' -> sometimes returns 502, sometimes 504 after ~10s. They say it started right after last night rollout (deploy bot shows deploy at 07:50 UTC).

Deploy Bot: deploy/redwood-api v2026.03.15-157 succeeded at 07:49:58 UTC (canary->prod).

Ethan - SRE: grabbing logs from edge/gateway now. Can you paste the exact error bodies if you have?

Priya - Support: Customer provided one sample error payload: 
```
{
  "error": "backend_error",
  "message": "failed to fetch cached KV prefix: cache timeout",
  "debug_id": "req_9f3b2c"
}
```
They also pasted a gateway log snippet: 
```
2026-03-15T08:15:03Z gateway ERROR request=req_9f3b2c upstream=cache-service timeout=10001ms code=504
2026-03-15T08:15:03Z gateway WARN request=req_9f3b2c fallback=miss route=/v1/generate
```

Marcos - Eng Runtime: prefix/KV cache used heavily for long-tail prompts to reuse KV cache between calls. If cache starts failing, runtime tries to fetch KV and can hang or bubble 5xx depending on circuit breaker.

Ethan - SRE: I'm seeing surge of connection timeouts to redis-cluster-01 in us-west-2: many ECONNRESET and socket timeout errors starting ~08:10 UTC. Metrics: connection_errors +1000 over 5m, cache_hit_rate dropped from 92% -> 40%.

SRE Bot: Alert: redis-cluster-01 replica lag > 30s; sentinel failover in progress.

Ethan - SRE: Ok that fits. Likely a Redis failover / replication storm causing connection churn and causing gateway to wait on KV fetch. Marcos can you confirm behavior on client side when redis ops block?

Marcos - Eng Runtime: On blocked KV calls we have a 5s socket timeout plus middleware that retries once; if both attempts blow past the request SLO we return 502/504 depending on where upstream fails. We also have a config toggle to bypass prefix caching at runtime.

Priya - Support: Customer is asking for ETA and mitigation. They've reported production impact on 6 endpoints.

Olivia - Customer Success: I'll message the customer with a short blurb: "we're investigating a cache dependency issue causing intermittent 5xx/timeouts; mitigation in progress, will follow up with update in 15 min".

Ethan - SRE: Short-term mitigation steps I'm applying now: 1) increase gate timeout for cache calls to avoid cascading timeouts (temporary), 2) enable client-side cache-bypass for prefix/KV for affected service slices, 3) scale up redis-read replicas and restart the unhealthy node. Applying step 2 now (flip config): 
```
kubectl patch cm redwood-runtime-config -n prod --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/prefix_cache/enable","value":false}]'
```

Marcos - Eng Runtime: A note — flipping prefix_cache to false will increase token cost (no KV reuse) and latency for cold prompts, but it will avoid cache-induced 5xx. I'll watch metrics.

Ethan - SRE: Restarted redis node redis-node-3. Logs showed OOM-kill; process restarted, but sentinel triggered failover which triggered many reconnections. We've mitigated OOM by adding swap and raising maxmemory policy. Still watching.

SRE Bot: Incident update: mitigation applied: prefix cache bypass enabled at 08:22 UTC, redis-node-3 restarted at 08:24 UTC.

Priya - Support: Customer updated: errors reduced but some requests still timeout. They're asking for permanent fix or rollback info.

Marcos - Eng Runtime: We're going to add a more defensive circuit breaker in runtime so a single cache outage doesn't stall request pipeline — that'll be a short-term patch in the next release. For immediate rollback: we can roll back last deploy which touched cache client behavior (v2026.03.15-157). But since Redis was also unstable, rollback may not fully return to previous state.

Ethan - SRE: Action items: 
- Ethan: stabilize redis cluster (scale, fix OOM, adjust eviction policy) — ETA 30m
- Marcos: monitor runtime error rates and keep prefix_cache disabled for now; prepare hotfix circuit-breaker — ETA 3h
- Priya/Olivia: update customer and open credit/billing review if SLA hit — ASAP
- Postmortem: assign after incident stabilized.

Priya - Support: I'll send the customer the ETA from Ethan and offer a phone bridge if they want.

Olivia - Customer Success: Shared customer note: "We have a mitigation in place; we expect full recovery within 30 minutes. We'll follow up with detailed root cause and any credits if SLAs were impacted." :phone:

Ethan - SRE: 08:39 UTC summary: cache error rate dropping, 5xxs down 85%, latency returning to normal. Leaving prefix_cache disabled until cluster fully healthy.

Marcos - Eng Runtime: Please keep me posted if any reproducible trace shows blocked stack frames in runtime. I'll instrument a trace to capture where KV calls block.

Priya - Support: Thanks everyone — closing the escalation thread for now. I'll reopen if customer reports more issues. Postmortem to follow with timeline + root cause (suspected: redis OOM -> sentinel failover -> connection churn -> runtime KV blocking -> API 5xx/timeouts). :white_check_mark:
